title: Does combining two exchanges improve the forecast?
finding: Across 27 matched state contests seven days out, the equal-weight forecast did not beat both venues on Brier score. These are correlated contests within one election, so this is a case study rather than a general platform ranking.

chart.title: Brier by horizon: the same 18 states at all three dates
chart.subtitle: This chart holds the cohort fixed at 18 states. The headline seven-day comparison uses all 27 available matched states. Lower Brier is better; one national election provides no estimate of performance across election cycles.

tables.title: Common-state cohort across horizons (lower Brier is better)
All available matched states and timestamp-age sensitivities

methods: Fixed target: Republican statewide winner in the 2024 US presidential election. Include every uniquely identified matching jurisdiction in the source panels; exclude Maine and Nebraska before looking at scores because of district electoral-vote rules.

Verify the exact party, state and election year against both official market rule records. No title-fuzzy matching and no winning-side selection. Both binary outcome directions are retained as original Republican YES prices, including below 51%.

Primary comparison: seven calendar days before election date, anchored to 2024-11-05 00:00 UTC. For horizon h use 2024-11-05 00:00 UTC minus h days (seven-day cutoff: October 29 00:00 UTC). Choose the latest retained source-panel observation no later than that common target, at most 24 hours old. The 1- and 14-day comparisons and 12-/6-hour age caps are declared sensitivities.
This uses actual completed_at timestamps, not each venue’s resolution date or the panel’s original days label. It therefore excludes the post-election January Kalshi settlement period.
The combination is fixed at 50% Kalshi plus 50% Polymarket before scoring. Report Brier scores on precisely the same state rows for all three forecasts.

The horizon chart holds the state cohort fixed across all three horizons. The primary seven-day comparison and timestamp-age sensitivities use every qualifying pair at their stated horizon; their sample sizes therefore differ.

No confidence interval or significance test is supplied: every state belongs to one shared national-election cluster. A reduction relative to the average component score is algebraically guaranteed for squared error; beating both components is the more demanding reported comparison.
limitations: Forecast target is matched but settlement mechanics are not identical: Polymarket permits three-network race calls with official certification as fallback; Kalshi closes after state certification. The prices need not be fungible or support arbitrage.

Common forecast cutoffs do not mean simultaneous transactions. Actual quote ages and cross-venue time gaps are reported, with stricter-age sensitivities. Prices are the latest available retained panel observation, not necessarily the latest exchange trade.
Only one election cycle. States are correlated and many safe states are easy; no general claim about which exchange is superior follows.
Trade prices include spreads and settlement timing/risk. This is forecast scoring, not after-fee trading profitability.
Current official metadata verifies targets and outcomes, but does not establish that contract wording never changed historically.

matches.name: Alaska
matches.polyRules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a Republican candidate wins the popular vote in Alaska in the 2024 US presidential election. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee, or has a ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable party preference, of the party in question.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.
matches.kalshiRules: If Donald Trump or another representative of the Republican party wins Alaska in the 2024 presidential election, then the market resolves to Yes.
matches.kalshiEarlyClose: This market will close following the state certification of election results.
matches.matchBasis: Exact state, 2024 election, Republican statewide winner; settlement source/timing differs

matches.name: Oregon
matches.polyRules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a Republican candidate wins the popular vote in Oregon in the 2024 US presidential election. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee, or has a ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable party preference, of the party in question.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.
